tours.name: Cash Sales Order
tours.description: Step-by-step guide to selling to a cash customer: create the quotation, confirm it, deliver the goods, invoice the customer and record the cash payment.

steps.title: Open the Sales app from the Odoo home screen to start a new sale
steps.content: Log in to Odoo. On the home screen you will see a grid of app icons. Find the **Sales** icon (a small bar-chart symbol) and click it. The Sales app opens, and its menu appears across the top of the screen.
steps.description: Why: every sale starts in the Sales app. Check: you should see the Quotations list afterwards. If the Sales tile is missing, your user has no Sales access, so ask your administrator.

steps.title: Click Orders in the top menu to see the order options
steps.content: Look at the menu bar at the top of the Sales screen (Orders, To Invoice, Products, Reporting, Configuration). Click **Orders**. A small dropdown opens below it.
steps.description: Why: the Orders menu groups quotations, sales orders and customers. Check: the dropdown shows Quotations and Orders.

steps.title: Click Quotations to open the list of all existing quotations
steps.content: In the dropdown, click **Quotations**. A list opens showing the quotations that already exist, with the customer, date and status of each.
steps.description: Why: a quotation is the draft of a sale. It becomes a Sales Order only after you click Confirm. Check: the list shows existing quotations with their status.

steps.title: Click New to start a blank quotation for the cash customer
steps.content: At the top left of the list, click the purple **New** button. A blank quotation form opens, and its title shows "New" until you save it.
steps.description: Why: a new form opens with number "New". The real number (for example S02213) is only given when you save. Tip: do not click Confirm yet, because the fields below must be filled first.

steps.title: Click the Customer field and type the customer's name to search for them
steps.content: On the form, find the **Customer** field near the top left. Click it and type the customer's name, or part of it. A list of matching customers appears below the field.
steps.description: Why: Odoo needs a customer to price the order and print the invoice. Tip: type at least 3 letters. You can search by name, phone or code. Watch out: if the customer does not exist, create them first (see the Create a Cash Customer manual).

steps.title: Select the correct customer from the search results list
steps.content: Look through the list and click the **correct customer**. The name now shows in the Customer field, and the Invoice Address and Delivery Address fill in by themselves.
steps.description: Check: the selected name appears in the field, and the Invoice Address and Delivery Address fill in automatically. Wrong customer? Click the field again and choose another one before saving.

steps.title: Set Order Payment Type to Cash because the customer pays immediately
steps.content: Find the **Order Payment Type** field. Click it and choose **Cash** from the choices. Choose Cash because the customer pays at the time of sale.
steps.description: Why: Cash tells Odoo the customer pays immediately, and it drives the invoice and payment steps at the end. Watch out: choosing Credit instead changes the later steps.

steps.title: Set Quotation Type to Sales to mark this as a normal product sale
steps.content: Find the **Quotation Type** field below it. Click it and choose **Sales**. This marks the order as a normal sale of products.
steps.description: Why: the Quotation Type separates normal sales from other order kinds (for example repairs or projects). Choose Sales for an ordinary product sale. Watch out: a wrong type can send the order to the wrong reports.

steps.title: Click Add a product to add a new row to the order lines
steps.content: Scroll down to the **Order Lines** table. Click the blue **Add a product** link at the bottom of the table. An empty row appears, ready to fill.
steps.description: Why: each row is one product. Tip: you can add several products by clicking Add a product again. Check: a new empty row appears in the order lines table.

steps.title: Type the product name or code in the new row to search for the product
steps.content: In the empty row, click the **Product** cell and type the product's name or code (for example 02BB 023). A list of matching products opens below the cell.
steps.description: Tip: you can type the product code or part of the name. Watch out: if the product list is empty, the product may be archived or not sellable (Can be Sold is off).

steps.title: Select the correct product from the search results
steps.content: Click the **correct product** in the list, for example [02BB 023] BALL BEARING 6202-2RS. Its description and unit price fill in on the row.
steps.description: Check: the product name, description and unit price fill in on the row. Watch out: if an error such as "no matching analytic account" appears, the product's category has no analytic account in the Product Group plan. Ask accounting to set the account's Product Category.

steps.title: Check the Quantity and change it if the customer is buying more than one
steps.content: Look at the **Quantity** column on the same row. It starts at 1. Click the cell and type another number if the customer is buying more. The line total updates by itself.
steps.description: Why: the quantity decides the price and what the delivery must hand over. Check: the line total (quantity x unit price) updates. Watch out: serial-tracked products need one serial number per unit, so keep the quantity at the number of serials you have in stock.

steps.title: Open the Other Info tab to fill in the payment, sales team and warehouse details
steps.content: Below the order lines, find the row of tabs (Order Lines, Optional Products, Other Info). Click the **Other Info** tab. It shows the payment, sales team and delivery fields.
steps.description: Important: in the next steps (14 to 21) the Payment Terms, Sales Team and Warehouse fields are usually filled in automatically by Odoo. Do not skip them. Check: look at each field and confirm the value is correct for this sale (Payment Terms = Immediate Payment, your own Sales Team, the warehouse that holds the stock). If a value is already correct, leave it and go to the next field. If it is empty or wrong, follow steps 14 to 21 to change it. Watch out: a wrong warehouse or team is the most common mistake, and it only shows up later on the delivery and the reports.

steps.title: Click the Payment Terms field to see the available payment terms
steps.content: In the **Payment Terms** field, click once. A list of payment terms opens (for example Immediate Payment, 30 Days, 90 Days).
steps.description: Why: payment terms decide when the customer must pay. Tip: the list shows only a few options, so type to search if yours is not listed.

steps.title: Select Immediate Payment because a cash sale is paid straight away
steps.content: Click **Immediate Payment** in the list. Do not choose terms such as "90 Days", because those create a credit sale and not a cash sale.
steps.description: Why: a cash sale is paid on the spot, so the invoice is due immediately. Watch out: terms like "90 Days" would create a credit invoice and break the cash flow.

steps.title: Click the Sales Team field to choose the team that is making this sale
steps.content: Find the **Sales Team** field and click it. A short list of teams opens. If your team is not in the list, use the next step.
steps.description: Why: the team groups the order for sales reports and targets. Tip: the field may already hold your default team, and you can leave it if it is correct.

steps.title: Click Search More... to see the full list of sales teams
steps.content: At the bottom of the short list, click **Search More...**. A window opens with all sales teams, so you can find yours quickly.
steps.description: Why: the short dropdown shows only a few teams. Search More... opens the full list in a window, where you can also search and filter.

steps.title: Select your own sales team from the list
steps.content: In the window, click **your own sales team** (for example Colombo Sales Centre). The window closes and the team name shows in the field.
steps.description: Check: the team name shows in the field after the window closes. Watch out: choose the team for the branch that is making the sale, because reports and commissions use it.

steps.title: Click the Warehouse field to choose where the goods will be shipped from
steps.content: Find the **Warehouse** field in the same tab and click it. A short list of warehouses opens. The warehouse is the place the goods will leave from.
steps.description: Why: the warehouse is where Odoo reserves and ships the stock from. Watch out: the wrong warehouse means the delivery is created in the wrong branch, and the stock may not be available.

steps.title: Click Search More... to see the full list of warehouses
steps.content: At the bottom of the list, click **Search More...** to open the window with all warehouses.
steps.description: Why: same as for the team, the full list helps you find the right branch quickly.

steps.title: Select the correct warehouse so the stock is taken from the right branch
steps.content: Click **the warehouse that holds the stock** (for example JAM Warehouse Ekala- (JM-EK)). The window closes and the name shows in the Warehouse field.
steps.description: Check: the warehouse name appears in the field. The product must be in stock here, or the delivery cannot be validated (a serial-tracked product also needs its serial number in this warehouse).

steps.title: Click Confirm to turn the quotation into a confirmed Sales Order
steps.content: Scroll to the top of the form. In the header, click the purple **Confirm** button. The status bar moves from Quotation to Sales Order, and new buttons such as **Delivery** appear.
steps.description: Why: confirming turns the quotation into a Sales Order and creates the delivery. Check: the status bar moves to Sales Order and a Delivery button appears. Watch out: if a purchase error such as "no matching vendor price" appears, the product's route is Buy / Make to Order and its Purchase tab needs a vendor line with a valid price and dates.

steps.title: Click the Delivery button at the top of the order to open the delivery document
steps.content: At the top of the sales order, click the **Delivery** smart button (a small box icon with a number). The delivery document opens, and its status should show Ready.
steps.description: Why: the delivery is the stock document that moves the goods out of the warehouse. Check: the delivery shows status Ready. If it is Waiting, the stock is not available yet.

steps.title: Click Validate on the delivery to confirm the goods were handed over to the customer
steps.content: In the header of the delivery, click the purple **Validate** button. Odoo records that the goods have left the warehouse, and the status changes to Done.
steps.description: Why: validating tells Odoo the goods have left the warehouse, and it reduces the stock. Watch out: a serial-tracked product asks for a Lot/Serial Number in Detailed Operations. If a locked order blocks validation ("Analytic Distribution"), open the sales order, click Unlock, then validate again.

steps.title: Click the order number at the top to go back to the sales order
steps.content: At the top left, click the **order number** (for example S01881) in the breadcrumb trail. You go back to the sales order.
steps.description: Why: the invoice is created from the sales order, not from the delivery. Check: the order now shows the Delivered quantity on its lines.

steps.title: Click Create Invoice on the sales order to start billing the customer
steps.content: In the header of the sales order, click **Create Invoice**. A small window opens that asks how you want to invoice.
steps.description: Why: this starts the billing wizard for the delivered goods. Check: a window opens that asks how to invoice.

steps.title: Click Create Invoice again in the pop-up window to confirm and create the invoice
steps.content: In the window, leave the default option (Regular invoice) and click **Create Invoice**. A draft invoice opens. If you see a **Confirm** button on it, click it so that the invoice is posted.
steps.description: Why: the default option Regular invoice is correct for a cash sale. Check: a draft invoice opens. Tip: check the amounts and the customer before going on.

steps.title: Click Register Payment on the invoice to record the cash received from the customer
steps.content: In the header of the invoice, click **Register Payment**. A window opens where you enter how the customer paid.
steps.description: Why: the invoice is only marked paid after a payment is recorded. Check: the invoice must be confirmed (posted) first. If you see a Confirm button, click it before registering the payment.

steps.title: Click the Journal field to choose where the payment will be recorded
steps.content: In the window, click the **Journal** field. A short list of journals (cash and bank accounts) opens.
steps.description: Why: the journal decides which account receives the money. For a cash sale it must be a cash journal, not a bank journal.

steps.title: Click Search More... to see the full list of journals
steps.content: At the bottom of the list, click **Search More...** to see every journal.
steps.description: Why: the dropdown may not list every journal, so Search More... shows the full list.

steps.title: Select Customer Receipts - Cash as the journal for this cash payment
steps.content: Click **Customer Receipts - Cash**. Check that the Amount equals the invoice total.
steps.description: Check: the Journal field shows Customer Receipts - Cash, and the amount equals the invoice total. Watch out: choosing a bank journal posts the money to the bank account instead.

steps.title: Click Create Payment to finish, and the invoice is now paid
steps.content: Click the purple **Create Payment** button. The window closes and the invoice is now paid.
steps.description: Why: this posts the payment and links it to the invoice. Check: the window closes and the invoice status changes to In Payment or Paid.

steps.title: Click the Sale Orders button to go back to the sales order
steps.content: At the top of the invoice, click the **Sale Orders** smart button. You go back to the sales order.
steps.description: Why: the order and the invoice are linked, so you can move between them. Check: the sales order shows the status Fully Invoiced.

steps.title: Click the Invoices button to open the invoice and check it one last time
steps.content: On the sales order, click the **Invoices** smart button to open the invoice again and check it one last time.
steps.description: Why: a last look confirms that everything is consistent: customer, amounts and status.

steps.title: Check the green In Payment ribbon, which shows the cash sale is complete
steps.content: Look at the top right of the invoice. A green **In Payment** ribbon means the payment has been recorded. The cash sale is now complete.
steps.description: Result: the cash sale is complete: order confirmed, goods delivered, invoice issued and payment recorded. Check: the green In Payment ribbon is on the invoice, and the order's smart buttons show one delivery and one invoice.
